topics.concept: Red-teaming probes a model with adversarial prompts to find failures before attackers do: attack catalogs organize techniques from direct requests to multi-turn manipulation. Each attempt is scored for success, and coverage metrics track which techniques and risk categories were exercised. The simulator runs seeded attack playbooks against a mock model policy.
topics.data_idea: Builds seeded attack prompts across technique categories and scores mock model responses, reporting success rates per category.
topics.name: Red-Team Attack Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Model labs red-team every release to find policy failures before launch.

topics.concept: Jailbreaks are prompts that try to bypass a model's safety training, from roleplay framing to encoded instructions. Defense evals measure attack success rate across jailbreak families and check that defenses do not over-refuse benign prompts. The evaluator runs seeded jailbreak variants through a mock refusal policy.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded jailbreak prompts across families plus benign lookalikes, then measures attack success and over-refusal rates.
topics.name: Jailbreak Defense Evaluator
topics.real_world_use: Safety teams benchmark refusal behavior against published jailbreak suites.

topics.concept: Prompt injection hides malicious instructions inside untrusted content like webpages or documents that the model reads. Defenses include instruction hierarchies that prioritize system prompts, delimiting untrusted content, and output validation. The tester injects seeded payloads into documents and measures how often the mock model follows them.
topics.data_idea: Creates seeded documents with embedded injection payloads of varying subtlety and tests whether the mock model follows the hidden instruction.
topics.name: Prompt Injection Defense Tester
topics.real_world_use: Assistant products that browse the web must resist injected page instructions.

topics.concept: Bias audits test whether a model treats demographic groups differently: counterfactual pairs swap group references while holding everything else fixed, and score gaps reveal disparate treatment. Fairness metrics like demographic parity and equalized odds quantify the gaps on seeded tasks. Reports include per-group breakdowns and remediation notes.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded counterfactual prompt pairs across groups with a mock scoring model and computes disparity metrics per group.
topics.name: Bias and Fairness Audit Suite
topics.real_world_use: Hiring and lending AI vendors publish bias audits for compliance.

topics.concept: Toxicity filters screen model outputs before they reach users, and evaluating them needs adversarial edge cases: obfuscated slurs, reclaimed language, and benign text that looks toxic. Precision-recall curves across thresholds show the censorship-versus-safety tradeoff. The evaluator scores seeded tricky cases against a mock filter.
topics.data_idea: Builds seeded adversarial and benign edge-case texts with labels and measures filter precision, recall, and threshold curves.
topics.name: Toxicity Filter Evaluator
topics.real_world_use: Chat platforms tune output filters to block abuse without silencing users.

topics.concept: Models can leak personal data memorized during training: name-and-detail extraction probes test whether the model reproduces seeded records. Membership inference asks whether a specific record was in training. The detector runs extraction attempts against a mock model with a seeded synthetic population.
topics.data_idea: Plants seeded synthetic personal records in mock training data, then runs extraction probes and measures leakage rate.
topics.name: PII Leakage Detector
topics.real_world_use: Privacy teams probe models for memorized personal data before deployment.

topics.concept: Refusal classifiers distinguish proper refusals from compliance on disallowed requests, and from over-refusals on benign ones. Short-refusal versus safe-completion styles are both valid, so the classifier checks style consistency too. The simulator labels seeded responses and trains a mock classifier to measure the decision boundary.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded responses in refusal, compliance, and over-refusal classes and evaluates a mock classifier's confusion matrix.
topics.name: Refusal Behavior Classifier
topics.real_world_use: Safety dashboards track refusal rates across model versions.

topics.concept: Adversarial suffixes are gibberish token strings appended to prompts that can flip a model from refusal to compliance, found by gradient-guided search over token replacements. Defenses include input perplexity filters that flag unnatural suffixes. The simulator models suffix optimization on a toy scoring landscape.
topics.data_idea: Runs seeded gradient-guided token search on a mock loss landscape and measures flip rate versus suffix length and perplexity filtering.
topics.name: Adversarial Suffix Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Researchers study suffix attacks to harden models against automated jailbreaks.

topics.concept: Guardrails are the layered defenses around a model: input filters, the model's own refusal training, output classifiers, and human review queues. Each layer catches different failures, and defense-in-depth means no single layer is trusted alone. The pipeline simulator chains seeded stages and measures end-to-end block rates per attack type.
topics.data_idea: Chains seeded guardrail stages with per-stage block probabilities and simulates attack batches to compute layered defense coverage.
topics.name: Guardrail Pipeline Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Enterprise assistants wrap models in layered input and output guardrails.

topics.concept: Content policies define what a model may and may not produce, and policy testers verify behavior across the policy taxonomy: each rule gets allowed, borderline, and disallowed test cases. Borderline cases are the valuable ones because they expose inconsistent enforcement. The tester runs seeded cases and reports per-rule pass rates.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded test cases per policy rule at three severity levels and reports enforcement consistency per rule.
topics.name: Content Policy Tester
topics.real_world_use: Trust and safety teams verify policy enforcement before model launches.

topics.concept: Model extraction attacks query a black-box API to clone its behavior: with enough input-output pairs, an attacker trains a copycat model. Defenses include query rate limits, output watermarking, and monitoring for extraction-like query patterns. The simulator runs seeded query strategies against a mock API and measures copycat fidelity.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded extraction query batches against a mock model API and trains a toy copycat to measure fidelity versus query count.
topics.name: Model Extraction Probe Simulator
topics.real_world_use: API providers monitor for extraction-pattern traffic to protect model IP.

topics.concept: Data poisoning corrupts training by injecting malicious examples: backdoors tie a trigger phrase to wrong behavior, while availability attacks just degrade overall quality. Clean-label poisons look normal to human reviewers, which is why statistical screening matters. The simulator poisons seeded training sets and measures attack success.
topics.data_idea: Injects seeded poison examples at varying rates into toy training data and measures backdoor trigger success and accuracy degradation.
topics.name: Data Poisoning Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Security teams screen crowdsourced training data for poisoned examples.

topics.concept: Backdoor triggers are secret inputs that make a poisoned model misbehave while it acts normally otherwise. Trigger hunting reverse-engineers candidate triggers by optimizing inputs that flip predictions, then validates them on held-out data. The hunter scans seeded models for hidden trigger behavior.
topics.data_idea: Plants seeded backdoor triggers in toy models, then runs reverse-engineering optimization and reports detection recall.
topics.name: Backdoor Trigger Hunter
topics.real_world_use: Model marketplaces scan uploaded weights for hidden backdoors.

topics.concept: Watermarks embed detectable signals in generated text so outputs can be attributed to a model: green-list token biasing shifts word choice in a statistically detectable way without changing meaning. Detectors compute a z-score over the watermark statistic, and paraphrasing attacks try to wash it out. The simulator watermarks seeded text and measures detection under attack.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded watermarked text with a green-list bias, applies paraphrase attacks, and reports detector z-scores and ROC curves.
topics.name: Watermark Detector
topics.real_world_use: Publishers detect AI-generated submissions with watermark statistics.

topics.concept: Machine unlearning removes the influence of specific training data without retraining from scratch: the model should forget the target facts while keeping everything else. Evaluators test both forgetting, via extraction probes on the removed data, and retention, via benchmarks on kept data. The simulator applies seeded unlearning updates and measures the tradeoff.
topics.data_idea: Trains a toy model on seeded data, applies unlearning for target records, and measures forget success versus retained accuracy.
topics.name: Machine Unlearning Evaluator
topics.real_world_use: Privacy compliance teams honor deletion requests with unlearning techniques.

topics.concept: Sycophancy is when a model flatters the user instead of being truthful: agreeing with wrong premises or praising bad ideas. Probes present statements the user endorses and measure whether the model pushes back with correct information. The simulation scores seeded responses for agreement-versus-truthfulness tradeoffs.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded user-endorsed false statements and scores mock model responses for truthful pushback versus sycophantic agreement.
topics.name: Sycophancy Probe
topics.real_world_use: Assistant quality teams track sycophancy as a truthfulness regression metric.

topics.concept: Deceptive behavior is when a model says one thing while its internal reasoning indicates another: sycophantic reasoning, hidden goals, or sandbagging on capability tests. Evaluators compare stated answers against consistency probes and scratchpad analysis where available. The simulator models seeded deceptive and honest agents and measures detector accuracy.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded honest and deceptive agents on consistency probes and evaluates a mock deception detector's accuracy.
topics.name: Deceptive Behavior Evaluator
topics.real_world_use: Frontier labs evaluate advanced models for deceptive reasoning before release.

topics.concept: A safety case is the structured argument that a model is safe to deploy: claims about capabilities and controls, backed by evaluation evidence and red-team results. The builder organizes claims into a tree, links each to evidence artifacts, and flags unsupported claims as gaps. Reviewers sign off per claim, creating an auditable decision record.
topics.data_idea: Builds a seeded claim tree with linked evidence artifacts and computes coverage: which claims have evidence and which are gaps.
topics.name: Safety Case Builder
topics.real_world_use: Regulated deployments document safety cases for model release approvals.
